clue.text: A yacht made in China

indicators.note: made here means made into something else, so the letters of the two words are reshaped

explanation.surface: A pleasure boat was built in a Chinese yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made in' looks like a label of origin, but 'made' is the anagram signal working on the letters of A YACHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathay is the old poetic and medieval European name for China.

clue.text: One stage act to correct drastically

indicators.note: drastically suggests a violent shake-up, so the letters are thoroughly rearranged

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A single theatrical act meant to reform someone harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drastically' looks like part of the definition but shuffles I (one) with STAGE ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Castigate originally meant to chastise or amend, to put right by punishment or revision.

clue.text: The jam-making trade

explanation.definitionFit: Vehicles on the road cause hold-ups, and commerce or dealing in goods is also so named.

clue.text: Made issue of ?

parts.note: issue here means a child, so the phrase describes a court fixing whose child a baby is

explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means offspring; in old law, to affiliate a child was to fix its paternity on a father.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to affiliate was to establish paternity, declaring a child the offspring of a named father.

clue.text: What this bird pays for footwear ?

definitions.text: What this bird pays for footwear ?

parts.words: What this bird pays for footwear ?
parts.note: read literally, the bill a bird would pay for its shoes; the bird is an African stork named for its huge clog-shaped beak

explanation.walkthrough: The bird's name splits into a piece of footwear and an invoice, though the 'bill' is really its beak.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoebill is a large African wading bird whose broad beak resembles a clog.

clue.text: Like 13, it's not the whole story

definitions.text: Like 13, it's not the whole story

parts.words: Like 13, it's not the whole story
parts.note: 13 across is only the second portion of a word meaning truthfulness, so it is a partial account

explanation.walkthrough: 13 across is the second half of VERACITY, a word for truth, so it is literally half of a truth.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement that is only partly true, leaving out the rest of the facts.

clue.text: She might climb almost all the mountain range

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means going upwards, so the letters are written bottom to top
almost all means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the Andes is the mountain range of South America

explanation.surface: A woman may scale nearly the whole of a great range.
explanation.walkthrough: ANDES loses its last letter under 'almost all' to give ANDE, which 'climb' turns upward into the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a woman's name, and a girl's name is fairly clued as 'she'.

clue.text: Drum III is made of this metal

indicators.note: what something is made of is the raw stuff, so these letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A drum numbered three is cast in some metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman numeral III is three letters I, and with DRUM they are rearranged into the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridium is a hard silvery-white metallic element of the platinum group.

clue.text: Like foals with horses in the grassland

indicators.note: in places the children's word for horses inside the field

parts.note: a ley is land temporarily under grass
gee-gees, GG, are horses in nursery language

explanation.surface: Young horses frisk in a meadow among older ones.
explanation.walkthrough: GG, nursery 'gee-gees' for horses, goes inside LEY, a field put down to grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Young horses have long thin limbs out of proportion to their bodies.

clue.text: The dam thing's almost uncanny!

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: weird means uncanny, strange

explanation.surface: A remark that the damned thing is almost spooky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dam' reads as a mild oath, but a weir is a low dam across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A weir is a low barrier built across a river to hold back water.

clue.text: Pinch a bit

explanation.definitionFit: To pinch is to steal or grab quickly; a snaffle is also a simple jointed mouthpiece for a horse's bridle.

clue.text: A stage between flights just arriving

explanation.definitionFit: A platform between two flights of stairs, and the act of an aircraft coming down to earth.

clue.text: Arrange to rent Flat II and enter unobtrusively

indicators.note: to arrange things is to put them in a new order, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out a lease on a second-floor flat and slips quietly in.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's '11' is the Roman numeral II, two letters I, which join RENT and FLAT as the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To infiltrate is to get into a place or group secretly, without being noticed.

clue.text: Vera's other 5 is a kind of editor

indicators.note: the other part is what remains of the word once the named piece is taken away

parts.note: 5 down is a half truth; truth is veracity, and its other half once the girl's name comes off is what is left
Vera is a girl's name, and also the first half of the word for truthfulness

explanation.surface: Gossip about Vera's other half and a newspaper editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Veracity means truth; split it into halves and Vera owns the first, so the other half of that truth is the rest. The cross-reference to 5 down supplies the idea of half a truth.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's financial editor is called its city editor, after the City of London.

clue.text: David's friend to act as guide on the river

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to steer is to guide
the Forth is the river of Edinburgh in Scotland

explanation.surface: A friend acts as a river pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: STEER sits 'on' FORTH, the Scottish river of Edinburgh. David is David Copperfield, whose charming, treacherous schoolfriend this is in Dickens's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: James Steerforth is David Copperfield's admired school friend in the Dickens novel.

clue.text: Old-fashioned artist retires with style without a following

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

indicators.note: without here has its old sense outside, so the stylish word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: chic means stylishness

explanation.surface: An outdated painter withdraws, still stylish but with no fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retires' turns RA into AR; 'without' means outside, so CHIC goes round A to make CHAIC, which follows AR. 'without a following' reads as having no fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic describes something belonging to an earlier time and now out of date.

clue.text: The water-clock rewound dry dry' places

indicators.note: rewound suggests something wound again in a new way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An old water-clock is reset in arid regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewound' fits a clock, but here it rearranges the letters of DRY PLACES.
explanation.definitionFit: A clepsydra is an ancient device measuring time by the flow of water.

clue.text: Like Kate firstly but not lastly

definitions.text: Like Kate firstly but not lastly

parts.words: Like Kate firstly but not lastly
parts.note: Kate is the shrew of Shakespeare's comedy about taming, wild at the start of the play and subdued by its end

explanation.walkthrough: Kate is Katharina in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew, wild at the start and subdued at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Untamed means wild and not yet brought under control, as Kate is before Petruchio subdues her.

clue.text: Assume as true indeed as laid down

indicators.note: the word indeed is split as in plus deed, telling the solver to put a piece inside that act

parts.note: taken as written, an act
to posit is to assume as true

explanation.surface: Accept something really as fixed by law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' splits as IN DEED: POSIT goes inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Deposited means put or set down, placed somewhere.

clue.text: Last term had trouble in the river

indicators.note: in places the jumbled word inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a common crossword river

indicators.note: a word that has had trouble has been knocked about, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The final school term was a difficult one down by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had trouble' turns TERM into TREM, which goes inside EXE, a river in Devon in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme in its older sense means outermost or final, the very last.

clue.text: It's material to get a ticket with a return half

parts.note: a tab is a ticket or tag

indicators.note: half points to the first half of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Buying a return ticket is relevant to the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'ticker' should be 'ticket'. TAB (ticket) and A are followed by RET, 'half' of RETURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabaret is an upholstery fabric with alternating silk stripes.

clue.text: The pale mixture not to be taken "?

indicators.note: a mixture stirs things together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A pale medicine bottle labelled not to be swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a medicine label; a heeltap is the dregs left in a glass, which one does not drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A heeltap is the dregs of liquor left in the bottom of a glass, which a drinker leaves undrunk.

clue.text: The subject's about right in global circles

indicators.note: about means the subject word goes round the next piece

parts.note: a topic is a subject, here with its 's

explanation.surface: The topic is roughly correct in international circles.
explanation.walkthrough: TOPIC'S goes 'about' R.
explanation.definitionFit: The two lines of latitude north and south of the equator are circles drawn round the globe.

clue.text: Stories of childhood

parts.note: stories here are a child's word for untruths, not tales told at bedtime

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stories' is a nursery euphemism for lies, so this is not about storybooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Small childish lies are told by children and called stories in the nursery.

clue.text: Such oak appropriate for a " fretted vault ?

definitions.text: Such oak appropriate for a " fretted vault ?

parts.words: Such oak appropriate for a " fretted vault ?
parts.note: a fretted vault is a carved ceiling, but fretted also means vexed, and a vexed person has steamed with anger

explanation.walkthrough: Oak darkened by ammonia fumes is a known finish; fretted also means angry, so the treated wood is apt for a fretted vault.
explanation.definitionFit: Fumed oak is oak darkened by exposure to ammonia; fumed also means seethed with anger.

clue.text: London docks quarantine area ?

explanation.definitionFit: A district of London's Docklands on a bend of the Thames; read literally, an island where imported pets are kept in isolation.

clue.text: Archdeacon is embarrassed by youth's first sin

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests being thrown into confusion, so the abbreviation is jumbled

parts.note: an archdeacon is addressed as the Venerable, Ven

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word youth

explanation.surface: A churchman is ashamed of a young person's first wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: VEN, the archdeacon's title Venerable, is jumbled by 'is embarrassed' into ENV, then Y, the 'first' letter of youth, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: No telling in this O.T. 13

parts.note: David's lament in the Old Testament begins by forbidding the news to be told in a Philistine city; 13 across is city

explanation.walkthrough: In 2 Samuel 1:20, David laments: 'Tell it not in Gath', a Philistine city of the Old Testament (O.T.); 13 across gives 'city'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gath was one of the five Philistine cities, Goliath's home town.

clue.text: Amphibian tavern

explanation.definitionFit: A sea-maiden lives in water yet can be on land; the Mermaid was the Elizabethan London tavern of Jonson and Shakespeare.

clue.text: Green holds back investigators finding the answer

indicators.note: holds means the colour word contains the next piece

parts.note: vert is green in heraldry

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read in reverse order

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: A green detective team finds the solution to a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CID into DIC, which 'holds' puts inside VERT. The CID is the detective branch of a British police force.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury's decision on the question put to it, its finding in the case.

clue.text: Airborne Wagnerian ?

parts.note: Wagner wrote an opera about a phantom sea captain whose ship is described as flying

explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's opera Der fliegende Holländer is The Flying Dutchman, so the airborne figure is its title character.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flying Dutchman is the spectral captain of Wagner's opera, cursed to sail forever.

clue.text: Went in pursuit of pure sound

indicators.note: sound tells the solver the word for pure is to be heard rather than written

parts.note: chaste means pure, virtuous

explanation.surface: Someone hunted down a clean, genuine noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pure sound' reads as a clean tone, but 'sound' says CHASTE is said aloud, giving the spelling of the past tense of chase.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase is to run after something, so chased is a past-tense synonym of pursued.
